divergesFromReason: Angular delegates Toast to Angular Material's MatSnackBar (frameworks/angular/behaviour-delegated.json), which has no tone axis at all -- so its binding stays the flat pattern "alert" it always was, while React's varies role and aria-live by tone and is cased. What MatSnackBar actually renders, read against the installed @angular/material 22.0.5 in node_modules/@angular/material/fesm2022/snack-bar.mjs: MatSnackBarConfig.politeness defaults to 'polite', the container resolves _live to 'assertive' only when politeness === 'assertive' && !announcementMessage, and _role is assigned ONLY inside `if (this._platform.FIREFOX)`. The template binds [attr.aria-live]="_live" [attr.role]="_role", so outside Firefox a snackbar carries aria-live="polite" and NO ROLE, whatever the message says. This divergence therefore has a cost to a real person rather than being merely structural: a critical error toast interrupts in React (role="alert", aria-live="assertive") and is queued in Angular. It is recorded and NOT decided, in components-divergences.md's "Toast -- a critical error interrupts in React and is queued in Angular", the same treatment Skeleton's divergence got. Note what this reason does NOT claim: behaviour-delegated.json's Toast entry binds `alert` with no exceptions while MatSnackBar renders no role, so that entry is inaccurate. It is left untouched on purpose -- that inaccuracy is pre-existing and belongs to CLAUDE.md's standing "every claim the delegated declarations make about Angular Material is unpinned" entry, and this binding must not stack a fresh claim on top of it.

exceptions.reason: Toast.jsx has no timer of its own, but its doc comment describes toasts as auto-dismissed by the host by default and `persist` as the opt-out. Nothing in this file enforces persist for a critical state, so the claim rests on the host.

cases.name: advisory
cases.when: any other tone -- role="status" with aria-live="polite"
